author: harness:claude-code

patch.value: The bunx release gate passes with an arbitrary token in the executable position, so the only Bun coverage in the pipeline cannot fail for the reason it exists

Post-publish verification runs three executor checks. Two are correct: npx --yes <pkg> --version invokes the default binary, and npx --yes --package <pkg> -- pm --version selects the named binary explicitly. The third is not: bunx --bun <pkg> pm --version passes pm as an argument to the already-selected default binary, where it is parsed as a command name. It only succeeds because --version is handled before command dispatch. Reproduced live against the published 2026.7.26: substituting a nonsense token for pm — bunx --bun @unbrained/pm-cli@2026.7.26 zzzbogus --version — prints the version and exits 0. The check therefore asserts nothing about which executable bunx resolved, and nothing about whether any command dispatches under Bun. Separately, the pipeline never exercises an install path for any manager: no global install, no project install, no bun add, no pnpm add. Bun compatibility is meanwhile real but undeclared — bun add @unbrained/pm-cli links all three binaries and pm init, pm create, and pm list all succeed under the Bun runtime, while the package declares only a Node engine range and no gate re-checks that.

The Bun check invokes the pm executable through an explicit selection mechanism, so a wrong or missing binary fails the check; A negative-control fixture proves the check fails when the executable is absent or misnamed, and that fixture runs in the pipeline rather than existing as documentation; The verified command exercises real dispatch rather than a flag handled before dispatch, so a runtime incompatibility surfaces; Install paths are verified alongside execution paths for every supported manager, including the global install that has produced field defects; The supported runtimes are stated explicitly in package metadata and documentation, and whatever is stated is what the pipeline verifies
Make the published-artifact checks capable of failing for the conditions they claim to cover
A gate that cannot fail is worse than no gate, because it is counted as coverage. This one guards the surface users touch first — the command that runs the tool immediately after publication.
A broken Bun entrypoint, a missing binary link, or a Bun-incompatible runtime change would publish and be advertised with every check green
Bun and npm are verified by execution and by installation, each with a control proving the check can fail
The daily release advertises on these checks, and the defect is a one-line invocation shape that costs nothing to correct

message: File bunx gate defect: reproduced bogus-token pass against published 2026.7.26; no install-path coverage for any manager

author: harness:claude-code
message: Record lineage: found while verifying the daily release-health surfaces end to end

value.author: harness:claude-code
value.text:
Positive control for the gate this item says cannot fail, run 2026-07-26 against the real published artifact rather than a bogus token.

  npx -y @unbrained/pm-cli@2026.7.26 --version   ->  2026.7.26
  bunx @unbrained/pm-cli@2026.7.26 --version     ->  2026.7.26

Both resolve, download, and execute the real package under their own runtime, from a clean temp directory with no prior cache. So the capability is genuinely there — which is exactly what makes the gate's weakness matter: a gate that also passes for zzzbogus is indistinguishable from this run, and this run is the outcome the gate is supposed to be asserting. Having both the true positive and the known false positive recorded on the same item gives the fix a two-sided test: the replacement gate must pass here and fail on the bogus name.

Also relevant to the item's second half, that no install path is exercised for any manager: neither of these invocations installs anything persistent. A real install-path assertion still has no coverage.

value.author: harness:claude-code
value.text: Functional counter-evidence recorded 2026-07-26 against the published 2026.7.26 artifact, using a real command sequence instead of a version short-circuit. In an isolated directory with sandboxed PM_PATH and PM_GLOBAL_PATH, bunx --bun @unbrained/pm-cli@latest ran init (exit 0, tracker created with prefix demo), then create (exit 0, returned id demo-jfxf), then list (exit 0, rendered the row). npx -y @unbrained/pm-cli@latest also resolved and executed. So Bun genuinely works end to end on the published tarball — the defect this item owns is entirely that the gate cannot observe it, not that the capability is missing. That distinction matters for the fix: the acceptance test should be exactly this create-then-read sequence under both runtimes, because it fails closed when resolution breaks, whereas any --version probe passes even with a bogus executable token.

value.author: harness:claude-code
value.text:
Verification (2026-07-28, against published 2026.7.28, bun 1.x, isolated HOME): Bun compatibility is real and now demonstrated beyond `--version`, which is the gap this item describes.

- `bunx @unbrained/pm-cli@latest --version` → `2026.7.28`
- `bunx @unbrained/pm-cli@latest init --yes` → completed, full settings envelope emitted
- `bunx @unbrained/pm-cli@latest create --title "bun smoke" --type Task` → `id: "pm-9hgh"`, `status: "open"`, `changed_field_count: 10`, exit 0

So a real command does dispatch under the Bun runtime — the thing the current gate asserts nothing about. npx is also green end-to-end (`npx -y @unbrained/pm-cli@latest --version` → `2026.7.28`).

That sharpens rather than weakens the item: Bun works, the gate still cannot prove it, and the package still declares only a Node engine range. A replacement gate should assert on a dispatched command's output, not on `--version`, since `--version` is handled before command dispatch and is exactly why the arbitrary-token substitution passes.
